faq.a1: Yes. There are no ads, no fees and no paid version. It is made by students of The Skyward Project.
faq.a2: Only the first time, to load the app and its reading tools. After that, most of Saath works without a connection.
faq.q3: Can it read Hindi or Marathi papers?
faq.a3: Yes. It reads printed papers in English, Hindi and Marathi. Handwriting is harder, so always check the numbers it finds.
faq.q4: What if my phone can’t speak my language?
faq.a4: Some phones don’t have a Hindi or Marathi voice. Saath will tell you, and you can still read everything on screen.
faq.q5: Will Saath tell me whether to take a loan?
faq.a5: No. Saath explains what the paper says and what it really costs. The choice is yours. Talk to someone you trust before you sign.

privacy.title: Privacy, in plain words
privacy.p1: Papers, photos and the words read from them never leave this phone. They are not stored on any server.
privacy.p2: Your account is a name and a password. Both stay in this browser, and the password is stored only in a scrambled form.
privacy.p3: If you switch on backup across phones, only four things are saved online: your tracker entries, your streak, your tasks and your path progress.
privacy.p4: Those four things are locked on your phone with your secret word before they are sent, so the server holds text that nobody can read.
privacy.p5: No ads. No tracking. No analytics. Nothing about you is sold or shared.
privacy.p6: You can delete an online backup and everything in it at any time, from your profile.
privacy.made: Made by The Skyward Project with the Interact Club of Pune Skyward.

intro.eyebrow: Your saathi for papers and money
intro.title: Understand a paper before you sign it.
intro.lead: Saath reads a loan or scheme paper and tells you, in plain words, what you will really pay. Then it helps you build money habits a few minutes a day.
intro.does: What Saath does, and how to use it
intro.s1P: Saath reads printed loan agreements, gold loan slips and government scheme forms in English, Hindi and Marathi. The photo is read on your phone and is never uploaded or kept.
intro.s1a: Open Scan from the bar at the bottom. Try one of the three sample papers first to see how it works.
intro.s1b: For your own paper, tap Use the camera. Lay the paper flat in good light. Saath tells you if the photo is blurry or dark.
intro.s1c: Check the numbers it found: amount, interest, months and fees. Each one shows the line from the paper beneath it. Fix anything that is wrong, then confirm.
intro.s2P: The result shows the total you will pay back as one large number, with the amount you borrow beneath it and a bar that separates the two. Four short blocks explain what you get, what you pay back, the real yearly cost and what happens if you pay late.
intro.s2a: Read What to watch. These are calm facts about the paper, most serious first, each with the exact line it came from.
intro.s2b: Open Questions to ask before you sign and take that list to the lender.
intro.s2c: Tap Ask about this document to ask in your own words, or Add to my tracker to follow the monthly payments in Money Lab. You can also share the explanation with family.
intro.s3P: Every result, lesson, case and question has a Listen button that reads it aloud in your language. It helps when reading is slow or tiring.
intro.s3a: Tap Listen. Tap it again to stop.
intro.s3b: On a scan result, each of the four blocks has its own Listen button, and one button reads the whole result.
intro.s3c: If your phone has no voice for your language, Saath says so and the words stay on screen.
intro.s4T: Three small tasks a day, and a streak
intro.s4P: Home shows three tasks chosen for today. Each takes under two minutes: answer a question, log an expense, read a lesson, check a fee or scan a sample.
intro.s4a: Tap a task to do it. It turns into a tick when it is done.
intro.s4b: Finishing even one task counts the day. The flame and the seven dots show your week.
intro.s4c: One missed day each week is forgiven automatically, so a day without your phone does not break your streak.
intro.s5P: A path is a guided set of five to seven steps on one skill. There are eight: First budget, Spot a loan scam, Read your first loan paper, Apply for a scholarship safely, Build a ₹1,000 emergency jar, Use UPI without fear, Understand your first salary slip, and Prepare for a bank visit.
intro.s5a: Pick a path on Home and tap Start. Steps are of three kinds: a short lesson, something to do in real life, and a quick check.
intro.s5b: When you have done a real-life step, come back and tap I did it.
intro.s5c: Finishing a path gives you a milestone card that you can share as text or as a picture.
intro.s6P: Money Lab is your tracker. It shows what is left this month, what came in, what went out and what you saved, with a simple chart of where spending went.
intro.s6a: Tap Log money, choose what it was, type the amount on the number pad and save. Two taps and a number.
intro.s6b: Set a savings goal and watch the ring fill. After three days of logging, Saath shows one thing about your own spending.
intro.s6c: Each week there is one real-life case to read and decide on. Loans you add from a scan appear here with their due dates.
intro.s7P: 25 short lessons on budgeting, loans, scams, savings, insurance, tax and ID. Each has a short introduction, three to five points, an example from real life, something to try and one question.
intro.s7a: Use the topic chips or the search box to find a lesson.
intro.s7b: Tap any underlined word to see what it means in simple language.
intro.s7c: Answer the question at the end to finish the lesson. That also counts toward your streak and your paths.
intro.s8P: You need an account to use Saath. It is a name and a password, kept on this phone. There is no email, no phone number, no ads and no tracking. Each account on a shared phone has its own tracker and progress.
intro.s8a: Tap the round button at the top right to change language, save a backup file, add a PIN or log out.
intro.s8b: Saath keeps working without internet after your first visit.
intro.s8c: Saath explains papers. It does not tell you whether to sign. Talk to someone you trust before you do.
